heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P achieves reliable structural prints with Bambu PETG-CF at speeds up to 179 mm/s backed by a 15 mm³/s max volumetric speed limit. However, the stock stainless steel nozzle and extruder gears will rapidly abrade, necessitating an upgrade to Bambu hardened steel components prior to printing.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with a thin layer of PVP glue stick or liquid glue as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap 'Max volumetric speed' at 15 mm³/s in the Filament settings to prevent under-extrusion at high motion rates.
Lower part cooling fan thresholds to Min 20% / Max 50% with fan disable for the first 3 layers to maximize interlayer bonding.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' set to 2 mm and configure 'Retraction distance' to 0.8 mm to suppress carbon-fiber nozzle drool.
Set 'Pressure Advance' to approximately 0.038 s (calibrated) and increase nozzle temperature to 255°C on a hardened steel hotend.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder gear slipping or rapid bore widening after a few prints
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Abrasive carbon fibers grinding against stock P1P stainless steel nozzle and drive gears.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install the Bambu Lab Hardened Steel Hotend (0.4mm or 0.6mm) and Hardened Steel Extruder Gear Assembly.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing, rough surface finish, and brittle layer adhesion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption by the hygroscopic PETG matrix inducing boiling and hydrolysis in the melt zone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a forced-air blast oven or active filament dryer at 65°C for at least 8 hours before printing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: PEI coating tear-out or permanent bonding to the build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG-CF molecularly bonding too aggressively to bare PEI surfaces without a separation barrier.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply Bambu Liquid Glue or standard PVP glue stick to the Textured PEI Plate to serve as a sacrificial release interface.

faq.question: Can I print Bambu PETG-CF with the factory-installed P1P nozzle?
faq.answer: No; the stock P1P nozzle is stainless steel, which will degrade and widen within 200–500 grams of carbon-fiber filament. You must install a hardened steel nozzle and hardened extruder gears.

faq.question: Does the open-frame Bambu P1P require an enclosure for PETG-CF?
faq.answer: No, PETG-CF does not require an enclosure and typically prints best in open, well-ventilated chambers to prevent heat creep and excessive chamber heat buildup.

faq.question: Can I use the Bambu 0.2mm nozzle for high-detail PETG-CF prints?
faq.answer: No, chopped carbon fiber strands will bridge across a 0.2mm orifice and cause immediate clogging. Use a 0.4mm or preferably 0.6mm hardened nozzle.

faq.question: Is Bambu PETG-CF compatible with the AMS on the P1P?
faq.answer: Yes, Bambu PETG-CF is formulated and wound on reusable spools to be AMS-compatible, but ensure the filament is thoroughly dried so it does not snap inside the feed paths.
